claim: PM2 is a daemon process manager (CLI, npm-installed) that keeps applications online: start/stop/restart/delete any script or binary, with process listing (pm2 ls), streaming logs (pm2 logs), and a terminal dashboard (pm2 monit).
quote: PM2 is a daemon process manager that will help you manage and keep your application online. ... it is offered as a simple and intuitive CLI, installable via NPM.
title: PM2 - Quick Start

claim: PM2 restart policy options include --watch (restart on file change), --max-memory-restart, --restart-delay <ms>, --cron <pattern> forced restart, and --no-autorestart — a broad restart-policy surface comparable to our backoff/autorun model but richer (memory cap, cron, watch).
quote:
--max-memory-restart 200M

# Set memory threshold for app reload

--log <log_path>
title: PM2 - Quick Start

claim: PM2 offers a web-based monitoring dashboard (pm2 plus / pm2.io) described as 'Web based dashboard, cross servers with diagnostic system' — the monitoring UI is a hosted SaaS add-on, not a local desktop panel.
quote: Web based dashboard, cross servers with diagnostic system
title: PM2 - Quick Start

claim: PM2 per-app env vars are declared in ecosystem.config.js with env and env_production blocks — env config exists but lives in a JS file, not an editable .env panel; PM2 has no port view or health_url probing.
title: PM2 - Quick Start

claim: PM2 handles boot persistence via 'pm2 startup' (generates an OS startup script) plus 'pm2 save' to freeze the process list for respawn — CLI-driven autorun, no GUI.
quote:
To solve this, just run this command to generate an active startup script:

$ pm2 startup

And to freeze a process list for automatic respawn:

$ pm2 save
title: PM2 - Quick Start

claim: NSSM runs any executable as a Windows service configured through a multi-tab GUI installer (Application, Details, Log on, Dependencies, Process, Shutdown, Exit actions, I/O, File rotation, Environment) — per-service config, not a multi-service dashboard.
quote: The installer consists of several tabs with lots of configurable parameters. Most are preset to nssm's defaults, so it's possible to install a service without leaving the Application tab.
title: NSSM - the Non-Sucking Service Manager

claim: NSSM implements exponential restart throttling: pause >=2000ms doubling per failure, max 256000ms (~4 min), reset after the app runs past the AppThrottle threshold (default 1500ms) — same backoff idea as our 2→5→10→20s restart policy.
quote: If the restarted application continues to exit before running for the threshold amount of milliseconds, nssm will pause for at least 2000 milliseconds, doubling the pause time for each subsequent failure. The maximum time it will pause is 256000 milliseconds, around four minutes.
title: NSSM - the Non-Sucking Service Manager

claim: NSSM supports per-exit-code exit actions (Restart/Ignore/Exit under AppExit), a mandatory AppRestartDelay between restarts, staged graceful shutdown (Control-C, WM_CLOSE, WM_QUIT, TerminateProcess), stdout/stderr redirection to files, and online log rotation.
quote: To configure the action which nssm should take when the application exits, edit the default value of the key HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\<servicename>\Parameters\AppExit. If the key does not exist in the registry when nssm runs it will create it and set the value to Restart. Change it to either Ignore or Exit to specify the action taken.
title: NSSM - the Non-Sucking Service Manager

claim: NSSM sets per-service environment variables via the Environment tab or AppEnvironment (replace) / AppEnvironmentExtra (add) registry values — env editing exists but only as raw KEY=VALUE lists per service, no cross-service overview.
quote: Environment variables set in AppEnvironmentExtra will be added to the service's default environment.
title: NSSM - the Non-Sucking Service Manager

claim: WinSW wraps a custom process as a Windows service driven by XML/YAML config files; CLI commands: install/uninstall/start/stop/stopwait/restart/status (status prints NonExistent/Started/Stopped); .NET-based, MIT license. No dashboard or multi-service view.
quote: WinSW is an executable binary, which can be used to wrap and manage a custom process as a Windows service.
title: Windows Service Wrapper in less restrictive license

claim: supervisord is a client/server process control system for UNIX-like systems that auto-restarts crashed subprocesses, provides a sparse web UI ([inet_http_server]) and an XML-RPC control API — but 'Supervisor will not run at all under any version of Windows,' leaving the Windows dev-supervisor gap open.
quote: Supervisor will not run at all under any version of Windows.
title: Introduction — Supervisor 4.3.0 documentation

claim: supervisord features: INI-style config, automatic restart of failed processes, automatic log rotation, process groups with priority-ordered start/stop ('start all'), and a web UI 'with functionality comparable to supervisorctl' — lifecycle management but no port monitoring or per-service env editor UI.
quote: Supervisor provides you with one place to start, stop, and monitor your processes. Processes can be controlled individually or in groups. You can configure Supervisor to provide a local or remote command line and web interface.
title: Introduction — Supervisor 4.3.0 documentation

claim: systemd.service offers the most granular restart taxonomy: Restart= takes no/on-success/on-failure/on-abnormal/on-watchdog/on-abort/always with an exit-cause matrix covering clean/unclean exits, signals, timeouts and watchdog misses; docs recommend on-failure for long-running services.
quote: Takes one of no, on-success, on-failure, on-abnormal, on-watchdog, on-abort, or always.
title: systemd.service — Service unit configuration

claim: systemd restart backoff: RestartSec= defaults to 100ms with RestartSteps= providing exponential growth toward RestartMaxDelaySec= ('values between 3 and 5 are good choices when exponential backoff is desired'); WatchdogSec= adds app-cooperative health via sd_notify WATCHDOG=1 keep-alives — unlike our external HTTP/TCP probe model.
quote: Configures the number of exponential steps to take to increase the interval of auto-restarts from RestartSec= to RestartMaxDelaySec=. Takes a positive integer or 0 to disable it. Defaults to 0. Hint: values between 3 and 5 are good choices when exponential backoff is desired.
title: systemd.service — Service unit configuration

claim: Docker Desktop Dashboard is 'a centralized interface to manage your containers, images, volumes, builds, Kubernetes resources, and logs' — the same single-pane pattern as our dashboard, but scoped to Docker containers only (no native processes).
quote: It provides a centralized interface to manage your containers, images, volumes, builds, Kubernetes resources, and logs.
title: Explore Docker Desktop

claim: Docker Desktop Containers view offers per-container start/stop/pause/resume/restart, real-time logs with search, 'Open the port exposed by the container in a browser', live CPU/memory/disk/network stat columns, bulk actions across Compose projects, and inspect showing port mapping — near feature-parity with our start/stop/logs/ports, minus autorun/env editing and limited to containers.
quote:
Start, stop, pause, resume, or restart containers
*   View image packages and CVEs
*   Delete containers
*   Open a terminal in the container
*   Open the port exposed by the container in a browser
title: Explore the Containers view in Docker Desktop

claim: Docker Desktop now surfaces AI diagnostics per row, flagging issues 'such as Container exited with an error or Container keeps restarting' — equivalent to our crash_loop issue/circuit-breaker UX appearing in a mainstream competitor.
quote: each row can surface AI-suggested diagnostic questions and flag detected issues, such as "Container exited with an error" or "Container keeps restarting."
title: Explore the Containers view in Docker Desktop

claim: Docker Desktop is free for small businesses (<250 employees AND <$10M revenue), personal use, education and non-commercial OSS; larger orgs need a paid Pro/Team/Business subscription.
quote:
Docker Desktop is free for:
    *   Small businesses (fewer than 250 employees AND less than $10 million in annual revenue)
    *   Personal use
    *   Education
    *   Non-commercial open source projects
title: Docker Desktop licensing

claim: Laravel Herd is a native (non-container) Windows+macOS dev environment: 'a fast, native PHP and Laravel stack for every project on your machine... manage everything in one place' — the closest desktop-GUI analog to our app, but PHP/Laravel-scoped.
quote: Herd gives you a fast, native PHP and Laravel stack for every project on your machine. Install it once and manage everything in one place without external dependencies.
title: Laravel Herd

claim: Herd's Services panel is the closest shipped analog to our service rows: each service shows name/version/port ('Redis ... v7.4.11 · Port 6379'), Start/Stop buttons, a 'Start Automatically' toggle, data directory, and per-service actions 'Documentation Open / Logs Open / Environment Variables' with .env values ready to copy.
quote: Run and manage local databases, caches, and other services alongside your sites.
title: Laravel Herd

claim: Herd's service-creation form includes 'Automatically start with Herd' and 'Default port in use' port-conflict detection; the app itself has 'Launch Herd at login — Start Herd automatically when you sign in to Windows' plus 'Start minimized as system tray application' — identical autorun+tray model to ours.
quote:
Launch Herd at login
Start Herd automatically when you sign in to Windows.
Start minimized as system tray application
Launch in the background, tucked into the system tray.
title: Laravel Herd

claim: Herd pricing: free tier 'No license needed'; Herd Pro $69/yr (list $99); Herd for Teams $199/yr (list $299, 10 licenses); lifetime Pro license offered. Pro adds managed services, deeper debugging, direct support.
quote:
### Herd Pro
The complete setup, zero hassle
$69 $99
Per year
title: Laravel Herd

claim: DevKinsta is a free, Docker-powered local WordPress suite for macOS/Windows/Ubuntu: one-click sites (Nginx, MariaDB, WP_DEBUG toggle, SMTP, DB manager) with push-to-Kinsta — site-centric, not a process supervisor; no ports/env/autorun model for arbitrary services.
quote: DevKinsta is free forever, and available for macOS, Windows, and Ubuntu. Used by 60,000+ developers, web designers, and freelancers.
title: Your Free Local WordPress Development Suite

claim: Local by WP Engine is a free desktop WordPress dev app: one-click WP installs with SSL, hot-swappable PHP versions, Live Links (shareable tunnel URLs), Local Connect push/pull to hosting, Cloud Backups — site-lifecycle tool, not a services dashboard.
quote:
Automatic WordPress installation
Local sets up WordPress for you. One click and your site is ready to go, SSL included!
title: Local — The #1 local WordPress development tool

claim: ServBay is a macOS/Windows local dev environment manager with 50+ one-click services (languages, DBs, DNS, SSL, mail, tunnels) and — most relevantly — a built-in MCP interface letting AI agents 'start, stop and restart services, install packages, switch language versions ... read logs and check ports' — the strongest MCP-overlap competitor to our direction.
quote: your agent can start services, create sites and query databases — built in, no setup, free.
location: FAQ — How does my AI agent connect
title: ServBay - AI-native local dev environment

claim: ServBay runs per-project environment/version lock ('Each project can lock its own language and database versions, isolated and switchable in one click') and sells Free (5 websites, 5 DNS records) / Pro (2 devices, unlimited sites, customizable HTTP/HTTPS ports) / Team (10 users) subscription tiers; exact $ prices are JS-rendered, not captured.
quote: Everything you need to get started is free. Upgrade for team-scale features — never metered per token.
title: ServBay - AI-native local dev environment

claim: XAMPP is a free Apache+MariaDB+PHP+Perl distribution for Windows/Linux/macOS whose control panel only does start/stop of the four bundled servers plus 'install these server as services' — the minimal ancestor of a services panel: no ports, no env, no health, no user-defined services.
quote: The XAMPP control panel for start/stop Apache, MySQL, FileZilla & Mercury or install these server as services.
title: XAMPP Windows FAQ

claim: Heimdall is an MIT-licensed PHP/Laravel web dashboard for organizing links to web applications; 'Enhanced apps' show live stats via each app's own API (e.g., NZBGet queue/download speed) — pure presentation layer with no start/stop, ports, env, or supervision.
quote: Enhanced apps allow you provide details to an apps API, allowing you to view live stats directly on the dashboad. For example, the NZBGet and Sabnzbd Enhanced apps will display the queue size and download speed while something is downloading.
title: Heimdall

claim: gethomepage is a YAML-configured (or docker-label-discovered) self-hosted dashboard with 100+ service widgets; health display is read-only: ICMP ping per host and siteMonitor (HTTP HEAD, fallback GET, shows response time) — it watches services but cannot control them.
quote: A modern, fast, secure fully proxied, highly customizable application dashboard with integrations for over 100 services and translations into multiple languages. Easily configured via YAML files or through docker label discovery.
title: homepage

claim: gethomepage's Docker integration binds service tiles to containers ('server: my-server / container: my-container') and expands live CPU/Memory/Network stats on click — display of container health/resources, still no start/stop control and no env/autorun.
quote: Clicking on the status label of a service with Docker integration enabled will expand the container stats, where you can see CPU, Memory, and Network activity.
title: Services — homepage docs

claim: Dashy is a free OSS homelab homepage (Docker or Node) with real-time status monitoring: 'App/Service status is checked by calling an URL and analyzing its HTTP response code. Host status is checked by sending a real ping ICMP request' — identical probe types to our health_url/ports checks, but display-only.
quote: App/Service status is checked by calling an URL and analyzing its HTTP response code. Host status is checked by sending a real ping ICMP request to the host.
title: Dashy

claim: Dashy polls status on a configurable interval ('Statuses are checked on page load, but you can allow continuous polling ... in seconds under appConfig.statusCheckInterval') and shows response time + status code on hover — the same probe-loop pattern as our 4s service probing, minus control actions.
quote: Statuses are checked on page load, but you can allow continuous polling by specifying a time interval between checks, in seconds under appConfig.statusCheckInterval and appConfig.pingCheckInterval.
title: Dashy

claim: VS Code's built-in port forwarding (Microsoft dev tunnels) gives a Ports view to expose a local service over the internet with private/public visibility and open-in-browser actions — it shares/encapsulates ports for a running session, rather than inventorying all listening ports or managing service lifecycle.
quote: Support for port forwarding is built into Visual Studio Code via Microsoft dev tunnels, no extension required. When running a local web service, you can use the Ports view to make the service accessible to others over the internet.
title: Port Forwarding

claim: VS Code launch.json configs carry entry point, args and environment variables, and compound launch configs start multiple configs together — a per-project, debugger-bound subset of our service specs: no restart policy, health probe, autorun, or port inventory.
quote: If your application requires a specific entry point, command-line arguments, environment variables, or another custom setup, create a launch.json configuration.
title: Debugging

claim: JetBrains run/debug configurations are 'a named set of startup properties that define what to execute and what parameters and environment should be used' — same named-service-with-env model as ours, but stored per IDE project, tied to run/debug sessions, with no OS autorun, port dashboard, or crash restart.
quote: Each configuration is a named set of startup properties that define what to execute and what parameters and environment should be used.
title: Run/debug configurations | IntelliJ IDEA

claim: Category boundary synthesis: process supervisors (PM2/NSSM/WinSW/supervisord/systemd) own lifecycle — restart policies, env, log capture, boot persistence — but are CLI/config-file tools with no GUI dashboard, no port view, no health probing, and (except PM2) no monitoring UI at all; none targets a Windows desktop UX for arbitrary dev services.
quote: Synthesis across sources 30–34: PM2 CLI+SaaS dashboard; NSSM/WinSW per-service SCM wrappers with registry/XML config; supervisord Unix-only sparse web UI; systemd Linux init with unit files.
title: multiple

claim: Category boundary synthesis: dev-environment managers (Docker Desktop, Herd, DevKinsta, Local, ServBay, XAMPP) ship real GUIs with start/stop+logs+ports, but manage only their own bundled stacks (containers, WP sites, PHP/DB runtimes) — none supervises arbitrary user processes across pet projects with per-service autorun and issue detection.
quote: Synthesis across sources 35–41: Docker=containers only; Herd/ServBay=bundled runtimes/DBs; DevKinsta/Local/XAMPP=WP/Apache stacks.
title: multiple

claim: Category boundary synthesis: home-lab dashboards (Heimdall/homepage/Dashy) have the best status-display patterns (HTTP HEAD probe w/ response time, ICMP ping, docker-label discovery, per-app API widgets) but are self-hosted web pages with zero process control — complementary display layer, not a lifecycle manager.
quote: Synthesis across sources 42–44: all three are browser start-pages showing links/status/widgets; no start/stop/restart capability exists in any of them.
title: multiple

claim: Differentiation hypothesis: our dashboard's defensible niche is the intersection — Windows-native GUI + arbitrary user processes (not containers/bundled runtimes) + port inventory + health probing + autorun-at-login + env overrides + issues — a combination no adjacent tool ships; closest single overlaps are PM2 (lifecycle breadth, CLI-only) and Herd Services panel (GUI pattern, PHP-scoped).
quote: Derived from feature matrices in W3-001..W3-035: each adjacent category covers ≤60% of our feature surface; the union leaves 'arbitrary-process supervisor with desktop GUI on Windows' uncovered.
title: multiple

claim: Feature gaps vs adjacent tools worth noting: PM2 has watch-restart/memory-cap/cron-restart we lack; systemd has exit-cause-aware restart taxonomy and watchdog protocol; homepage/Dashy have response-time display and docker-label auto-discovery; Docker Desktop has CPU/mem stat columns and AI issue flagging; ServBay/Herd have per-project version pinning and MCP service control.
title: multiple
